newsitem.title: USA: Dow stumbles back to negative, tech stocks sturdy.
newsitem.headline: Dow stumbles back to negative, tech stocks sturdy.

text.p: The Dow industrials slipped to negative ground on Wednesday, stumbling again after a second push higher towards the 8,000. But technology stocks were resilient, helped by Motorola Inc's results.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 32 points, or 0.40 percent, to 7929, after hitting a session high of 7991.
It pulled back as the long bond also eased from session highs to trade up 7/32 at a 6.56 percent yield.
"A lot of people are selling right below the 8,000 level," Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co, said. "It (the 8,000 level on the Dow) is seen as an asset realocation point..."
Charlie Crane, managing director of Avatar Associates, said he was surprised the broader market was not stronger given the strength in the bond market.

Technology stocks also drifted from highs but remained stronger than the broader market. The Nasdaq composite rose two points to 1487, as the sector was boosted by above-forecast results from technology giant Motorola.
